method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Acute scrotal pain or swelling' (Last updated January 2026), retrieved 2026-09-23. claims.claim: ⚠️ **Testicular torsion and irreducible hernia are emergencies** — if suspected, get urgent surgical evaluation.
claims.source_text: Testicular torsion and irreducible hernia are emergencies and if suspected, require urgent surgical evaluation
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute scrotal pain or swelling' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_scrotal_pain_or_swelling/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Ultrasound only in selected cases, after surgical assessment**, so management is not delayed.
claims.source_text: Ultrasound should only be considered in selected cases of testicular pain, after surgical assessment, to avoid delays in management
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute scrotal pain or swelling' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_scrotal_pain_or_swelling/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Scrotal trauma or bruising — especially in infants or with an unclear mechanism — should prompt consideration of child abuse.**
claims.source_text: Scrotal trauma/bruising, especially in infants or where the causal mechanism is unclear, should prompt the clinician to consider child abuse
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute scrotal pain or swelling' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_scrotal_pain_or_swelling/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Commonest causes:** torsion of the testicular appendage, epididymitis and testicular torsion.
claims.source_text: The most common causes of acute scrotal pain and/or swelling are torsion of the testicular appendage (appendix testis), epididymitis and testicular torsion
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute scrotal pain or swelling' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_scrotal_pain_or_swelling/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Delay costs testes: torsion treated within 4 to 6 hours has 80 to 100 percent viability.** Even with a delayed presentation, still seek an urgent surgical opinion.
claims.source_text: Delays in surgical management of testicular torsion result in higher rates of testicular loss. Torsion within 4 to 6 hours: 80 to 100 percent viability … Although viability is low with delayed presentations, urgent surgical opinion should still be sought
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute scrotal pain or swelling' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_scrotal_pain_or_swelling/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pain may be referred to the testis** from the abdomen (appendicitis, renal colic, UTI) or the hip; scrotal skin infections (cellulitis, shingles) and **Henoch-Schönlein purpura** can also cause pain and swelling.
claims.source_text: Pain may be referred to the testes from other sites, including intraabdominal: appendicitis/renal colic/UTI referred hip pain Skin infections of the scrotum cellulitis/shingles Testicular pain and swelling can occur in Henoch-Schönlein purpura secondary to vasculitis in the scrotum
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute scrotal pain or swelling' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_scrotal_pain_or_swelling/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not delay surgical review for investigations.** Blood tests, ultrasound and Doppler are **not useful in the acute setting** (except for trauma).
claims.source_text: Surgical review should not be delayed in the interest of investigations Blood tests, ultrasound and doppler ultrasound are not useful in the acute setting (excluding traumatic injuries)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute scrotal pain or swelling' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_scrotal_pain_or_swelling/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **A negative ultrasound does not exclude torsion** — findings may be non-specific, and scanning may delay surgery and cost the testis.
claims.source_text: findings may not be specific to torsion and negative ultrasound has been documented in cases of torsion May also cause delay to definitive surgical management, affecting the viability of the testis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute scrotal pain or swelling' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_scrotal_pain_or_swelling/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Only once torsion and irreducible hernia are excluded** may ultrasound be considered if the diagnosis is still unclear.
claims.source_text: Once testicular torsion and irreducible hernia have been excluded, ultrasound may be considered if the diagnosis remains unclear
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute scrotal pain or swelling' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_scrotal_pain_or_swelling/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Suspected epididymo-orchitis:** urine MCS (ideally first-pass). Bacterial infection is more likely with structural urinary tract abnormality, recent instrumentation or an STI. **A normal urine does not exclude it.** Chlamydia and gonorrhoea PCR if an STI is suspected.
claims.source_text: For suspected epididymo-orchitis Urine MCS (ideally first pass urine collection) Bacterial infection more likely in child with structural urinary tract abnormalities, recent instrumentation of urinary tract, or STI A normal urine does not exclude epididymo-orchitis Urine Chlamydia and Gonorrhoea PCR testing (if STI clinically suspected)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute scrotal pain or swelling' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_scrotal_pain_or_swelling/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Viral causes** include enterovirus, adenovirus and rarely mumps (orchitis 4-6 days after parotitis); if mumps is suspected, send RT-PCR and/or IgM.
claims.source_text: Viral causes include enterovirus, adenovirus and rarely mumps (mumps orchitis occurs 4-6 days after parotitis). If mumps is suspected: RT-PCR and/or IgM
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute scrotal pain or swelling' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_scrotal_pain_or_swelling/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider urinalysis (nephrotic syndrome) and urine MCS.**
claims.source_text: Consider urinalysis (nephrotic syndrome) and urine MCS
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute scrotal pain or swelling' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_scrotal_pain_or_swelling/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Testicular torsion — suspected or not confidently excluded: urgent surgical review.** Fast (nil by mouth or sips of clear fluid per local guideline) until review, and give adequate analgesia.
claims.source_text: Testicular torsion If suspected, or cannot be confidently excluded, urgent surgical review Fast (nil by mouth or sips of clear fluid per local guideline) until surgical review Provide adequate analgesia
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute scrotal pain or swelling' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_scrotal_pain_or_swelling/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Irreducible hernia — if you cannot reduce it: urgent surgical review**, fast, and consider a nasogastric tube on free drainage if bowel obstruction is suspected.
claims.source_text: Irreducible hernia If unable to reduce, urgent surgical review Fast (nil by mouth or sips of clear fluid per local guideline) until surgical review Consider a nasogastric tube on free drainage if bowel obstruction is suspected
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute scrotal pain or swelling' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_scrotal_pain_or_swelling/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Torsion of the testicular appendage** can be hard to tell from testicular torsion — **explore surgically if torsion cannot be confidently excluded.** Once confirmed, treat supportively with analgesia and rest; pain should settle in 5-10 days.
claims.source_text: Torsion of testicular appendage May be difficult to distinguish from testicular torsion Requires surgical exploration if unable to confidently exclude testicular torsion Once diagnosis confirmed, treatment is supportive, with analgesia and rest Pain should resolve in 5-10 days
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute scrotal pain or swelling' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_scrotal_pain_or_swelling/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Trauma: surgical review for all testicular trauma**, unless the testis is clearly normal and not significantly tender. For suspected abuse, follow the child abuse pathway.
claims.source_text: Trauma Surgical review for all testicular trauma, unless the testis is clearly felt to be normal and without significant tenderness In cases of suspected child abuse presenting with testicular or scrotal trauma, see Child abuse
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute scrotal pain or swelling' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_scrotal_pain_or_swelling/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Suspected epididymo-orchitis: antibiotics IV if systemically unwell or a young infant, oral if well.** A second episode warrants renal tract ultrasound and urological review. Discomfort and swelling may take weeks to subside.
claims.source_text: Suspected epididymo-orchitis Antibiotics: IV if systemically unwell/young infant, oral if well Second episode: renal tract ultrasound and urological review May have weeks of gradually subsiding scrotal discomfort and swelling
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute scrotal pain or swelling' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_scrotal_pain_or_swelling/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hydrocele:** 90% resolve spontaneously by 2 years; consider outpatient surgical referral if still present after 2 years of age. **Varicocele:** refer to surgical outpatients.
claims.source_text: Hydrocele 90% resolve spontaneously by 2 years Consider outpatient surgical referral for repair if present after 2 years of age Varicocele Refer to surgical outpatients
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute scrotal pain or swelling' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_scrotal_pain_or_swelling/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Scrotal oedema** can accompany systemic disease such as nephrotic syndrome; if idiopathic, it resolves spontaneously over 1-5 days with no intervention.
claims.source_text: Scrotal oedema Scrotal oedema can occur in setting of systemic disease eg nephrotic syndrome If idiopathic, resolves spontaneously over 1-5 days. No intervention required
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute scrotal pain or swelling' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_scrotal_pain_or_swelling/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consult the surgical team urgently in every case where testicular torsion cannot be confidently excluded.** Involve the paediatric team if child abuse is suspected.
claims.source_text: Consider consultation with local surgical team in all cases where testicular torsion cannot be confidently excluded (urgently) Consider consultation with local paediatric team in cases of suspected child abuse
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute scrotal pain or swelling' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_scrotal_pain_or_swelling/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Transfer if surgical management is unavailable locally.**
claims.source_text: Consider transfer when Surgical management unavailable at local hospital
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute scrotal pain or swelling' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_scrotal_pain_or_swelling/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge once surgical advice has been given** and a follow-up plan and review (if needed) are in place.
claims.source_text: Consider discharge when Surgical advice has been provided Follow up plan in place and review scheduled (if required)
